thread:
alex.k: Ran a small A/B this morning comparing flash_v2 fused-matmul prefill vs paged-fusion prefetch on 16k seqs. Seeing a weird tail regression on decode small-batches, dumping notes.

jordan: Can you paste the exact config you used (batcher, kv page size, kernel flags)?

alex.k: Sure — full command and config I ran:
```
./run_bench --model llama2 --workload mix-2-64 
  --batcher continuous --prefill_kernel fused-matmul --decode_kernel small-decode-v2 
  --kv_page_size 512 --flash_variant flash_v2_blocking --quant none
```

mai: Nice. What are the perf numbers (p50/p95/p99) and throughput delta? :thinking:

alex.k: p50 decode 3.1ms, p95 8.7ms, p99 18.4ms. Prefill p99 ~6ms. Overall token throughput down ~9% compared to baseline (small-decode-v1 + paged-opt).

perf-bot: Profile summary for thread 1823456789: top stall sources: KV page eviction 28%, kernel launch overhead 14%, warp divergence 9%. Hot funcs: kv_page_fetch(), fused_attention_forward(). Flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/1823456789 :eyes:

sam: KV page eviction that high smells like allocator/pinning issue. Did continuous batching combine heterogenous seq lengths so prefill didn't populate correct pages for decode?

alex.k: That's my hypothesis. When the batcher merges short (2-token) and long (64-token) requests the prefill uses different page patterns; decode threads then remap pages and we see rematerialize/eviction. Repro is deterministic when mixing 25% short, 75% long.

jordan: Can you try forcing decode kernel to paged-opt with kv_prefetch enabled and measure p99?

alex.k: I tried that: p99 drops from 18.4ms -> 10.2ms, throughput still -4%. Also noticed flash_v2_blocking gives better steady throughput but increases tail due to launch serialization on small-batch decode.

mai: Suggested short-term mitigation: revert automatic kernel selection for decode to small-decode-v1 on Dedicated until we fix allocator heuristics. Medium-term: implement batcher-aware kv-page allocator + prefill->decode page pinning.

alex.k: Agreed. I'll open RFC + repro scripts (includes the small mixed workload). Quick repro command: `./run_bench --model llama2 --workload mix-2-64 --kernel prefill:fused-matmul,decode:small-decode-v2 --kv-page 512`

sam: Thanks. Also add a perf test that tears down and warms kv pages between runs to validate the eviction path.

alex.k: Will do. Filing follow-ups: RFC #3421 (kv-page allocator), PR draft for conservative decode kernel selection, and a perf job on the flaky fleet. TLDR: tail due to kv page thrash + kernel launch serialization for flash_v2 on tiny decode batches. :thumbsup:
